summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 25%), chronic systolic heart failure, ICD in place, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and tobacco use was admitted for acute shortness of breath and congestion. He presented with a two-day history of worsening dyspnea and mild weight gain, without chest pain or fever. Evaluation revealed elevated BNP (2468) and mild interstitial edema on chest X-ray, consistent with an acute exacerbation of heart failure. He was treated with intravenous furosemide, resulting in significant diuresis and clinical improvement. Oral torsemide replaced furosemide, and spironolactone was added for long-term management. Warfarin was reduced to 3 mg daily due to an elevated INR, and imipramine was tapered to 25 mg nightly. Anemia related to chronic kidney disease was addressed with iron supplementation. The patient stabilized, was weaned off supplemental oxygen, and discharged home with medication adjustments and close follow-up arranged with cardiology and primary care.
